myths.Agent_1:
Long before humans walked the valleys, the mountains were guarded by a spirit named Aella. She possessed a heart woven from morning mist, yet she bore a terrible sorrow: she had no voice. While the rivers babbled and the winds howled, Aella could only listen in absolute silence.

One twilight, the arrogant god of thunder, Taranis, rested upon her peak. He boasted loudly to the stars, his voice shaking the stone. As he slept, Aella crept forward and stole a single breath from his parted lips, hoping to finally sing.

When Taranis awoke, he discovered the theft. Furious, he summoned a blinding storm and cornered the trembling spirit. "You dare steal the sound of the heavens?" he roared.

Aella opened her mouth to plead, but the stolen breath rebelled. Instead of her own thoughts, she could only cry out, "The heavens!"

"You shall never speak for yourself," Taranis cursed her, his eyes flashing with cruel lightning. "You will only ever repeat what is given to you."

To this day, Aella wanders the high, lonely crags and deep caverns. Whenever a traveler shouts into the void, she eagerly catches their words, calling them back, forever borrowing voices, forever seeking her own.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, before the mountains had voices, the world was wrapped in a heavy, unbroken silence. The wind blew, but it made no sound. The rivers flowed, but their rushing was mute. Among the silent peaks lived Aethel, a spirit of the air, who longed to hear the beauty of her own existence. 

Aethel possessed a wondrous gift: a flute carved from the first fallen star. When she played, the melody was so profound that the sky wept colors, yet the earth absorbed the notes instantly, leaving nothing behind. Desperate to share her song, she sought the Great Stone Titan, slumbering beneath the crags. 

"Awaken," she mimed, offering her flute. The Titan, moved by the silent plea, struck a bargain. He would grant the mountains a memory, allowing them to hold onto her music, but in exchange, Aethel must bind her spirit to the canyons forever. 

She agreed without hesitation. She played one final, piercing note. The rock fractured, catching the sound, bouncing it from cliff to cliff. Aethel vanished into the mist, becoming the invisible voice. Now, whenever a wanderer shouts into the void, Aethel answers, repeating their call so the world never forgets how to sing a song.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long ago, the deep canyons were realms of absolute silence. Aethel, a lonely spirit woven from morning mist, wandered these chasms, longing to join the chorus of the world. But having no lungs, she possessed no breath, and therefore no voice.

One evening, a fierce storm shattered a sacred thunder-tree, leaving behind a perfectly hollowed branch. Aethel carved it into a magnificent flute, hoping its magic would allow her to finally sing. Yet, no matter how hard she tried to play, her misty form simply passed through the wood. 

Desperate, she sought out the Mountain King, a colossal being of living stone. "I have the instrument, but lack the breath," she mimed. 

The King proposed a bittersweet pact. "I will bind you to the canyon walls. You will remain unseen, but whenever a traveler passes and shouts into the void, you may catch their breath to play your flute. However, you can only ever play the exact notes they give you."

Aethel agreed. She faded into the rock, clutching her wooden prize. Now, whenever a voice rings out in the mountains, Aethel eagerly catches the sound, playing it back through her flute, forever borrowing the breath of mortals to make her music.

Aella’s misty form vanished into the crags. To this day, the invisible spirit wanders the canyons. Whenever a wanderer shouts into the void, Aella answers, forever catching their words and throwing them back.

When Boreas awoke, he immediately sensed the theft of his wind. Furious, he summoned a terrifying gale and cornered the poor, trembling spirit.

"You dare steal the breath of the sky?" he thundered.

"Since you borrow the voices of others," Boreas cursed, his eyes flashing, "you shall be bound to these rocks forever."

Aethel's misty form vanished into the jagged crags. Now, whenever a lonely traveler shouts into the deep valleys, the invisible spirit eagerly catches their breath, playing it back through her wooden flute.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Before the world possessed the gift of song, the deep ravines were suffocated by a crushing, absolute silence. Aella, a solitary phantom woven from the silver morning mist, drifted through the barren gorges. Desperate to weave melodies into the stillness, she shaped a delicate flute from the shimmering shards of a fallen star. Yet, as a being of vapor, Aella had no breath to awaken the instrument.

One evening, Taranis, the imperious god of storms, settled upon her highest precipice to sleep. His rumbling exhales caused the very mountains to shudder. Driven by her insatiable craving for music, Aella crept near and trapped a single, tempestuous breath inside her crystalline reed.

Upon waking, Taranis immediately realized his divine wind had been poached. Enraged, he conjured a swirling cyclone, trapping the fragile spirit.

"You dare siphon the breath of the skies?" he roared.

Aella lifted her flute to beg for mercy, but the trapped storm-wind refused to yield. The enchanted reed simply regurgitated the god’s furious question, hurling the words back against the stone walls.

"If you must steal to speak," Taranis condemned, "become the stone and speak only what is spoken to you!"

Aella dissolved into the canyon walls. Today, whenever a traveler shouts into the gorge, the captive spirit catches their voice, desperately trying to weave it into her eternal song.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Before the world knew illusions, the great deserts were domains of absolute, blazing truth. Aella, a lonely spirit woven from the heat waves, wandered the endless dunes, yearning to fill the barren wastes with beauty. From the polished remains of a fallen sun-shard, she carved a magnificent, shimmering mirror. Yet, possessing no physical body, the heat-spirit had no form to reflect.

One high noon, the arrogant god of rain descended to rest upon her highest dune, bringing with him visions of lush, emerald oases and cool waters. As he slumbered, Aella crept forward and captured a single, vibrant reflection of his watery dream within her sun-glass.

When the rain god awoke, he immediately sensed the theft of his divine vision. Furious, he summoned a scorching wind, cornering the trembling spirit. "You dare steal the waters of heaven?" he thundered.

Aella raised the mirror to plead, but the stolen vision rebelled. The magical glass merely projected the god's own paradise onto the horizon, forever out of reach.

"Since you borrow the visions of others," he cursed, "you shall be bound to these sands forever!"

Aella vanished into the heat. Now, whenever a thirsty traveler wanders the desert, the invisible spirit eagerly catches their deepest desires, playing them back through her sun-mirror as a shimmering, untouchable oasis.
